title: The best players aged 25 and under still in the Champions League
content:
It is time for Europe’s best to go head-to-head in the knockout phase of the Champions League.

On Tuesday and Wednesday, the round of 16 gets underway and with the continent’s powerhouses still in contention special moments will likely be required from special players to decide who progresses.

Legends are made in the knockout phase, so who are the game-changers and who could play a big part in the games to come?

Taking into account league-phase form, here are 10 players aged 25 and under to keep an eye on this week.

Gordon’s attacking versatility means he has been used as Newcastle’s No 9, as well as in his usual position on the left wing, to great effect. With summer signing Yoane Wissa missing much of the season with injury and Nick Woltemade taking up deeper positions, Gordon has proved to be Newcastle’s talisman in the competition.

The Newcastle winger has registered 10 goals in 10 games so far, helped by being the team’s penalty taker. Last month, he became the first player to score four goals in the first half of a knockout game, scoring in his team’s 6-1 first-leg play-off win over Qarabag.

“I think there’s more to come from him,” said Newcastle manager Eddie Howe after their Champions League victory over Benfica in October. “The challenge for him, and all the players, is to produce it on a consistent basis, because if he can, there are very few who can do what he can.”

They call him a robot for good reason. The Manchester City No 9 makes few errors in front of goal and makes scoring look routine. His power and speed, combined with his clever off-ball movement, help the Norwegian get into threatening areas, even if he doesn’t always get many touches beforehand.

While he has been off the beat at times in the Premier League this season, his numbers are still among the best on the continent. His seven goals in eight appearances in the Champions League put him joint-fourth in the competition’s scoring charts.

“Haaland is a special striker. Because he’s so strong, he’s quick, he’s got all the attributes to make a defender’s life very difficult,” said Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk in an interview with Sky Sports in October 2021.

Szoboszlai’s ability to shoot from distance and his free kicks make him a serious goalscoring threat from midfield. With four goals, he is Liverpool’s leading scorer in the competition. As seen below, two of his three non-penalty goals have been from outside the box from an xG of just 1.6.

As well as his goals, Szoboszlai has four assists in eight games. This included the winning penalty in a 1-0 over Inter and a Ronaldinho-esque free kick against Marseille as he slid the ball under the opposition wall.

“He’s just a natural-born football player,” former team-mate Trent Alexander-Arnold told Bleacher Report in October 2023. “They can kind of do everything, and it’s just natural… He’s a very special talent, he’s an exceptional player and a great lad as well.”

It is joyous watching Vinicius Junior in full flow. The Brazilian has completed 62 dribbles in the Champions League, with only Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal more successful, and can be relied upon as Real Madrid’s main goal threat on the left or through the middle.

Vincius Jr scored in both legs of the play-off against Benfica to help Real Madrid progress to the round of 16, with his second-leg goal decisive. The first leg had been overshadowed by alleged racist abused suffered by the Madrid goalscorer, who has three goals and four assists across 10 games in this season’s competition.

“Vinicius? When he plays like he did today, with such freedom and lightness … what can I say? I didn’t even touch him, and it wasn’t out of respect. He’s so quick, so hard to mark,” said Olympiacos defender Rodinei to TNT Sports after the teams met in November and Vinicius got two assists in a 4-3 Madrid victory.

Doue won the Golden Boy 2025 award for his efforts in PSG’s Champions League-winning campaign last season, earning the man-of-the-match award in the 5-0 win over Inter in the final. Though he started the season with injury problems, his directness and willingness to progress the ball helped PSG overcome Monaco 5-4 on aggregate in the play-offs.

PSG were 2-0 down to domestic rivals Monaco in the first round of the play-offs before Doue came on as a substitute in the 27th minute. The French winger scored twice, while Achraf Hakimi rebounded in from a Doue saved shot, as PSG completed a 3-2 comeback win. Despite entering the game almost half an hour in, only one player had more progressive carries than Doue, as seen below.

“I’m happy to go on record: I think he’s a Ballon d’Or winner in the future — within the next five years,” said TNT Sports pundit and former Chelsea and England forward Joe Cole after the Monaco game. “He’s such a superb player. I love watching him play. He gets you off your feet. When he came on, he just completely changed the game.”

One of the main beneficiaries of underlapping runs, the left-back has blistering pace with a recorded top speed of 35 kilometres per hour this Champions League campaign. His underlapping runs help PSG play out of pressure and launch more direct attacks, and he is skilled both on the ball and in recovering defensively.

The defender’s willingness to get forward has yielded two goals and two assists in 10 appearances. Only four players have made more ball recoveries than Mendes’ 65 and he’s completed over 600 passes, showing confidence in possession.

“When you play against a team that is always pressing high, having players like Nuno who can overcome that pressure with dribbling or passing, who can make runs in behind, helps you,” PSG head coach Luis Enrique said after an away win against Barcelona in November.

The winger’s attacking output this season at Bayern Munich has been sensational — 10 goals and 16 assists in the Bundesliga alone.

His tight control, dribbling and vision make him a hard player to defend against. With a wicked left foot, his in-swinging crosses — from both open play and corners — have caused problems for the opposition in the Champions League, as seen below.

Though he did not shine in defeats by Arsenal and PSG, Olise has one goal and four assists overall this season. His best game statistically came in September’s 4-1 win over Pafos, when he registered a goal and two assists.

“I certainly expect him to get even better. I’ve seen the development of talents like him many times,” said Bayern manager Vincent Kompany after the opening Bundesliga match in August.

“I see total calmness in Michael. He comes up to us because he wants to get even better.”

Like Vinicius Jr, the teenager glides past players. He’s completed the most dribbles in this year’s Champions League and undoubtedly he’s Barcelona’s main man when they need a special match-deciding moment. Last month, in a La Liga match against Villarreal, he scored his first career hat-trick to hint that even better things are to come from the 18-year-old.

Three goals and three assists in six games means he has a goal contribution per game. But in Barcelona’s toughest games, defeats against PSG and Chelsea, he wasn’t able to influence the result.

“Among the most talented prospects the club has ever had, nobody has had the scrutiny and pressure Lamine is facing,” one executive source told The Athletic earlier this month. “When Messi had his age, he had just burst onto the scene and had other stars, such as Ronaldinho or Samuel Eto’o, who would take the blame when needed. Now, all eyes are on Lamine. For the good and the bad.”

The defensive midfielder’s ability to read play and break up opposition attacks, while also being technically strong in possession, is a valuable asset. The graphic below shows how Caicedo’s 40 recoveries, with 25 coming in the middle of the pitch, has helped Chelsea gain control of games. Only one player has made more tackles than Caicedo’s 33 in the competition.

Caicedo was awarded man of the match in Chelsea’s 1-0 win over Pafos in January, scoring the winning goal. He also scored a goal in their comprehensive 5-1 victory over Ajax in October.

“He’s the best midfielder in the league,” said Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville in October, after Caicedo’s superb goal in the 2-1 win over Liverpool in the Premier League.

While Arsenal boast the best defence in Europe, their most reliable attacking option is Saka. Gabriel Martinelli has been the in-form Arsenal forward in the Champions League, with six goals in seven games, but it is Saka that the club will rely on in the later rounds. The one-club man is a selfless star who leads by example, with commendable work rate. His creativity has seen him used in the No 10 role this season, as well as his usual position on the right wing.

He scored two goals and two assists in the league phase. But those stats are likely to improve should Arsenal progress further, especially as they are on the favourable side of the knockout bracket. More goals and assists could come against Bayer Leverkusen on Wednesday.

“Bukayo was good but he wasn’t the talk of the academy. That’s why I have a lot of respect for Bukayo, he’s my favourite player,” Arsenal great Thierry Henry said on BBC Sport’s Football Focus in 2024. “I never thought we would see the levels we are seeing. The evolution of his game is just outstanding.”
